rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read walad with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām in four Maryam positions, al-Zukhruf, and Nūḥ, six in all.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ولدا بضم الواو وسكون اللام في هذه السورة أربعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basrans, Ibn Kathīr, and Khalaf use the rounded form only in Sūrat Nūḥ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير وخلف في سورة نوح بالضم فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All remaining readers use fatḥa on both wāw and lām throughout the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الواو واللام في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a Banū Asad proverb as evidence for the singular use of walad.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء من أمثال بني أسد

rows.speaker: معاذ الخرشي
rows.claim: Muʿādh al-Khurashī maintains that walad is only plural and cites a poetic line that seems to use it as singular.
rows.anchor: وكان معاذ الخرشي يقول لا يكون الولد إلا جمعا وهذا واحد يعني الذي في المثل

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects Muʿādh’s restriction: walad may be plural or singular, like other paired forms, and the cited verse proves singular use.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون جمعا كأسد وأسد ويجوز أن يكون واحدا فيكون ولد وولد كحزن وحزن وعرب وعرب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the poet’s phrase walad ḥimār shows singular usage, like fulk, which can be singular or plural.
rows.anchor: وليت فلانا كان ولد حمار يدل على أنه واحد ليس بجمع فهو مثل الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In afaraʾayta, the relative clause is the first object of raʾayta and the interrogative clause aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb is the second.
rows.anchor: الموصول هو المفعول الأول لرأيت والاستفهام في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats kallā as rebuke, restraint, and alert: it should stop and awaken the speaker to his error.
rows.anchor: كلا زجر وردع وتنبيه أي هذا مما يرتدع به وينبه على وجه الضلالة فيه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows kallā to connect with what follows, as in kallā wa-rabbi al-kaʿbah.
rows.anchor: يكون صلة لما بعدها كقولك كلا ورب الكعبة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Qurʾānic kallā has two senses, negation and an attention marker akin to illā, with some contexts admitting both readings.
rows.anchor: جاءت في القرآن على وجهين بمعنى لا يكون ذلك وبمعنى إلا التي للتنبيه

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim says both senses can apply in some places and notes that kallā can also begin a fresh statement, as in al-ʿAlaq 96:6.
rows.anchor: وجاءت في مواضع متوجهة على التأويلين ويدل على ذلك أنها قد تكون مبتدأة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses kallā in a rebuking response before continuing the assertion.
rows.anchor: كلا زعمتم بأنا لا نقاتلكم إنا لأمثالكم يا قومنا قتل

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says one should not pause at kallā because it is an answer whose point comes in what follows.
rows.anchor: لا يوقف على كلا لأنها جواب والفائدة تقع فيما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view permits pausing at kallā; the source notes that stopping on it is among the Qurʾān’s difficult pause questions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يجوز الوقف عليه. ومن مشكلات الوقف في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies ten kallā locations as good both for pausing and restarting when kallā rejects what came before; if it means an alert or affirmation, one restarts there.
rows.anchor: أحدها: ما يحسن الوقف عليه ويحسن الابتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-category examples include the covenant and idol-honor passages, plus examples about return, partners, escape, gardens, increase, scripture, divine dishonor, and wealth preserving life.
rows.anchor: أم اتخذوا عند الرحمان عهدا كلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These examples can take either analysis: kallā rejects the preceding statement, or it begins a new alert or emphatic statement.
rows.anchor: فمن جعل كلا في هذه المواضع ردا للأول بمعنى لا ليس الأمر كذلك وقف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two locations allow pausing after kallā but not restarting there: responses after speakers fear they will be killed or overtaken.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني: وهو ما يحسن الوقف عليه ولا يحسن الابتداء به فموضعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nineteen locations allow restarting at kallā but not pausing after it, because it does not reject the preceding statement.
rows.anchor: وأما الثالث: وهو ما يحسن الابتداء به ولا يحسن الوقف عليه فتسعة عشر موضعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some authorities allow pausing at kallā throughout the Qurʾān as an alert, except before the oath kallā wa-l-qamar, which is joined to the oath.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إنه يحسن الوقف على كلا في جميع القرآن لأنه بمعنى انتبه إلا في موضع واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At two locations beginning with thumma kallā, neither particle takes a pause because thumma is conjunctive and the meaning follows both particles.
rows.anchor: لا يحسن الوقف على ثم لأنه حرف عطف ولا على كلا لأن الفائدة فيما بعد هذين الحرفين

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: A report identified as sound says al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil owed Khabbāb money and refused payment unless Khabbāb renounced Muḥammad; Khabbāb refused until death and resurrection.
rows.anchor: روي في الصحيح عن خباب بن الأرت قال كنت رجلا غنيا وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين

rows.speaker: العاص بن وائل
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ claimed he would be resurrected with wealth and children and repay Khabbāb then; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: فسوف أقضيك دينك إذا رجعت إلى مال وولد قال فنزلت الآية

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains God’s increase in guidance as guidance through the abrogating revelation after the abrogated one.
rows.anchor: يزيد الله الذين اهتدوا بالمنسوخ هدى بالناسخ عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God increases guidance by enabling obedience, granting success in seeking His pleasure, opening proofs, and giving subtle helps that draw people toward good deeds.
rows.anchor: يزيدهم هدى بالمعونة على طاعاته والتوفيق لابتغاء مرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting righteous deeds outlast their doers through their reward and benefit their owners in this world and the next, surpassing the status of which opponents boast.
rows.anchor: الأعمال الصالحة التي تبقى ببقاء ثوابها وتنفع صاحبها في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr maraddan means a better outcome and benefit: good work is returned by God as reward after its doer has lost it through death.
rows.anchor: خير عاقبة ومنفعة يقال هذا الشيء أرد عليك أي أنفع وأعود عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afaraʾayta expresses amazement at the denier of God’s proofs, whether Qurʾānic or other proofs; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify him as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
rows.anchor: أفرأيت كلمة تعجيب ومعناه أرأيت هذا الكافر الذي كفر بأدلتنا من القرآن وغيره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the denier as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الوليد بن المغيرة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads the example generally: it applies to anyone with this trait.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عام فيمن له هذه الصفة عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the promise of wealth and children is sarcastic: the man boasts that he will receive them in Paradise.
rows.anchor: استهزاء أي لأعطين مالا وولدا في الجنة عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he means he will receive wealth and children in this life if he stays with his fathers’ religion and worship of idols.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعطي في الدنيا أي إن أقمت على دين أبائي وعبادة آلهتي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid take the question as asking whether the man knows the unseen well enough to know if he is destined for Paradise.
rows.anchor: أعلم الغيب حتى يعلم أهو في الجنة أم لا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the man claims to have looked into the Preserved Tablet and learned that wealth and children will be granted him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ عن الكلبي وتأويله أشرف على علم الغيب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains the covenant as a good deed the man previously offered to God.
rows.anchor: اتخذ عند الله عهدا بعمل صالح قدمه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the covenant to mean that God promised the man admission to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أم عهد الله إليه أنه يدخل الجنة عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the covenant is confession of God’s oneness, through which God may show mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أم قال لا إله إلا الله فيرحمه الله بها عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects his claim that he will receive wealth and children, or denies that he knows the unseen or holds a covenant with God.
rows.anchor: أي ليس الأمر على ما قال من أنه يؤتى المال والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will instruct the recording angels to register what he says so that he is requited for it in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: سنأمر الحفظة بإثباته عليه لنجازيه به في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will add punishment to punishment, linking its parts so that it never ends; the verbal noun intensifies the verb like repetition does.
rows.anchor: نصل له بعض العذاب بالبعض ونزيده عذابا فوق العذاب فلا ينقطع عذابه أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd say God will inherit the man’s wealth and children by destroying him and nullifying his ownership.
rows.anchor: ما عنده من المال والولد بإهلاكنا إياه وإبطال ملكه عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will come to the Hereafter alone, without wealth, children, support, or numbers.
rows.anchor: يأتي الآخرة وحيدا بلا مال ولا ولد ولا عدة ولا عدد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The idolaters chose gods to serve as intercessors in the Hereafter; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses their hope as protection from God.
rows.anchor: ليكونوا لهم شفعاء في الآخرة عن الفراء وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس ليمنعوهم مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hoped the idols would intercede and support them, imagining that the idols would bring them honor.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم رجوا منها الشفاعة والنصرة والمراد ليصيروا بهم إلى العز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā denies that the idols brought honor: instead, they brought their worshippers humiliation and punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ليس الأمر كما ظنوا بل صاروا بهم إلى الذل والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters will disavow the idols after seeing the evil outcome and deny having been polytheists.
rows.anchor: ويقولون والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī instead says the worshipped beings will deny the idolaters’ worship and call them liars, as in the statement that they had not worshipped them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن المعبودين سيكفرون بعبادة المشركين له ويكذبونهم فيها

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash notes that ḍidd can be singular or plural; here the idols aid the idolaters’ enemies, oppose them, and dispute with them.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش الضد يكون واحدا وجمعا كالرسول والعدو ومعناه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the idols will be companions with the idolaters in Hell, cursing and disowning them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ويكونون قرناء لهم في النار ويلعنونهم ويتبرؤون منهم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī says the idols will be the idolaters’ enemies on Judgment Day, although they were their allies in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ويكونون أعداءهم يوم القيامة وكانوا في الدنيا أولياءهم عن القتيبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In a noncanonical report from Qatāda via al-Ḥasan, the verbs are read in the passive, yuḥsharu and yusāqu.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ رواية قتادة عن الحسن يحشر المتقون ويساق المجرمون

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads shayʾan iddan with fatḥa on the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقراءة السلمي شيئا أدا بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وحفص
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, and Ḥafṣ read takādu with tāʾ and yatafattarna with tāʾ and a doubled, fatḥa ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وحفص تكاد بالتاء يتفطرن بالتاء وفتح الطاء مشددة

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read yakādu with yāʾ and yatafattarna in both sūrahs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي يكاد بالياء يتفطرن في السورتين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر وهبيرة عن حفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, Hubayra from Ḥafṣ, and Yaʿqūb read takādu, yanfaṭirna, with nūn and kasra on ṭāʾ in both sūrahs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر وهبيرة عن حفص ويعقوب تكاد بالتاء ينفطرن بالياء والنون وكسر الطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة وخلف
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and Khalaf read takādu yanfaṭirna here; in ʿAsq they read takādu yatafattarna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة وخلف ها هنا تكاد بالتاء ينفطرن بالنون مثل أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive readings of being gathered and driven are supported by the phrasing in al-Zumar 39:71.
rows.anchor: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-udd with fatḥa means force; on this reading, idd means something possessing force, or it can be an adjective used substantively.
rows.anchor: والأد بالفتح القوة قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rajaz line uses udd for force and supports this lexical sense.
rows.anchor: نضوت عني شرة وأدا فعلى هذا يمكن أن يكون المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infiṭār is the intransitive of fatarahu, while tafattur follows tafṭīr and carries a stronger, repeated-action sense that better suits the context.
rows.anchor: والانفطار مطاوعة الفطر يقال فطره فانفطر والتفطر مطاوعة التفطير

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan understands takādu as ‘intend’; he gives the same sense for kādnā li-Yūsuf and akādu ukhīhā.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو الحسن في معنى قوله تكاد السماوات إلى أن معنى تكاد تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended split need not occur or even approach: the heavens only mean to split in horrified response to the polytheists’ claim.
rows.anchor: يردن لا أنهن ينفطرن ولا يدنون من ذلك ولكن من هممن به إعظاما لقول المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative rhetorical explanation says Arabs magnify a lie or outrage by saying that the earth nearly split; the outrageous claim about God is compared with the greatest imaginable disaster.
rows.anchor: كانت العرب إذا سمعت كذبا أو منكرا تعاظمته وعظمته بالمثل الذي عندها عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī introduces Arabic poetic parallels to this hyperbolic way of describing an outrage.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي ومما يقرب من هذا قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation gives three poetic hyperboles: a split sky over al-Ḥārith, Mecca bristling as though no Hāshim remained, and Medina’s walls and mountains bowing at news of al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: على ابن لبينى الحارث بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izz means disturbance impelling someone toward an action; azzahu describes agitating him, while a pot’s azīz is its boiling sound.
rows.anchor: الإز الإزعاج إلى الأمر يقال أزه يأزه وأزيزا إذا هزه بالإزعاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes the Prophet praying with his chest sounding like a boiling cauldron because of weeping.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث أنه كان يصلي وأزيز جوفه كأزيز المرجل من البكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb azaztu can mean that one thing was joined or pressed to another.
rows.anchor: وأززت الشيء إلى الشيء ضممته إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafd is a collective for a delegation, with wufūd as another plural; wafada means to come as a delegate, and awfada means to rise above something.
rows.anchor: والوفد جمع وافد وقد يجمع وفودا أيضا وفد يفد وفدا وأوفد على الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root s-w-q means urging onward; sāqahu is to drive, the leg carries forward motion, and a market is named for successive buying and selling being driven along.
rows.anchor: والسوق الحث على السير ساقه يسوقه سوقا ومنه الساق لاستمرار السير بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ward is a group that comes to water, from warada, to arrive at water.
rows.anchor: والورد الجماعة التي ترد الماء يقال ورد الماء يرد وردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idd means a momentous matter, as witnessed by a rajaz line using iddan for a great calamity.
rows.anchor: والإد الأمر العظيم قال الراجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infiṭār is splitting, tafattur is splitting or cracking, and hadd is demolition with a forceful sound.
rows.anchor: والانفطار الانشقاق والتفطر التشقق والهد الهدم بشدة صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuʾizzuhum is a circumstantial clause; the object of naʿuddu is omitted and understood as their deeds.
rows.anchor: تؤزهم جملة في موضع الحال ومفعول نعد لهم محذوف والتقدير نعد أعمالهم عدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm naḥshuru can be attached to naʿuddu, or to the statement that they have no power of intercession on that day.
rows.anchor: ويوم نحشر ظرف قوله نعد لهم ويجوز أن ينتصب بقوله لا يملكون الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafdan and wirdan are accusative circumstantial complements describing the Godfearing as delegations and the criminals as those driven to water.
rows.anchor: وفدا منصوب على الحال من المتقين أي وافدين ووردا كذلك أي واردين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception in illā man is either a nominative relative clause substituting for the subject of yamlikūn, or an accusative disconnected exception because covenant-holders are not criminals.
rows.anchor: إلا من اتخذ هو موصول وصلة في موضع رفع لأنه بدل من الواو في يملكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s splitting is coordinated with the earlier clause with an implied takādu; the mountains’ falling is explained as an infinitive or a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وقوله تنشق الأرض جملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها وتقديره وتكاد الأرض تنشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase an daʿaw is a causal complement: because they ascribed a child to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وأن دعوا مفعول له والتقدير لأن دعوا أي لأجل ذلك

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains sending satans as God leaving unbelievers among them when they whisper and call people to error, without coercively preventing them; sending is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: خلينا بينهم وبين الشياطين إذا وسوسوا إليهم ودعوهم إلى الضلال حتى أغووهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor is like saying that someone released his dog upon another person.
rows.anchor: كما يقال لمن خلى بين الكلب وغيره أرسل كلبه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God empowered satans over unbelievers, which likewise means leaving them to their influence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه سلطناهم عليهم ويكون في معنى التخلية أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the satans agitate unbelievers away from obedience and toward sin.
rows.anchor: تزعجهم إزعاجا من الطاعة إلى المعصية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the satans incite people to evil, urging them onward until they fall into Hell.
rows.anchor: تغريهم إغراء بالشر تقول امض امض في هذا الأمر حتى توقعهم في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should be at ease and not hasten punishment: the unbelievers’ remaining time is short, and its days and years are being counted down.
rows.anchor: فلتطب نفسك يا محمد ولا تستعجل لهم العذاب فإن مدة بقائهم قليلة فإنا نعد لهم الأيام والسنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās alternatively says God counts their breaths in this life until the appointed term of punishment; this is a powerful threat.
rows.anchor: نعد أنفاسهم في الدنيا فهي معدودة إلى الأجل الذي أجلناه لعذابهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that God is counting their deeds, as explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه نعد أعمالهم على ما ذكرناه قبل

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the Godfearing are brought to the Merciful as delegations and groups, toward Paradise and the abode of honor.
rows.anchor: إلى الرحمان أي إلى جنته ودار كرامته وفودا وجماعات عن الأخفش

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās says they ride unprecedented camels with golden saddles and emerald reins until they reach Paradise’s gates.
rows.anchor: ركبانا يؤتون بنوق لم ير مثلها عليها رحائل الذهب وأزمتها الزبرجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda say criminals are driven on foot, parched like camels arriving at water; ward names their thirst-driven arrival.
rows.anchor: ونحث المجرمين على المسير إلى جهنم عطاشا كالإبل التي ترد عطاشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals can neither intercede nor have another’s intercession take effect for them; these are the two senses of possessing intercession.
rows.anchor: فلا يشفعون ولا يشفع لهم حين يشفع أهل الإيمان بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms of intercession are pleading for someone else and requesting another’s intercession for oneself; neither is available to these unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لأن ملك الشفاعة على وجهين أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may mean that only covenant-holders possess intercession, or that intercession is made only for them.
rows.anchor: أي لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition of the covenant is faith, confessing God’s oneness, and affirming His messengers.
rows.anchor: والعهد هو الإيمان والإقرار بوحدانية الله تعالى وتصديق أنبيائه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the covenant is the shahāda, disowning one’s own power, and hoping only in God.
rows.anchor: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن يتبرأ إلى الله من الحول والقوة ولا يرجو إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view limits intercession to those whom God promised to authorize, including prophets, martyrs, scholars, and believers, as reports state.
rows.anchor: وعد له الرحمان بإطلاق الشفاعة كالأنبياء والشهداء والعلماء والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
rows.claim: A report in ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm’s tafsīr, through his father and al-Ṣādiq’s family, transmits the Prophet’s instruction that a dying person make a covenant and testify to core beliefs.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم في تفسيره

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet’s deathbed covenant affirms God, Muḥammad, Paradise, Hell, resurrection, judgment, decree, the scales, the revealed religion, Islam, and the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: إني أعهد إليك في دار الدنيا إني أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت وحدك لا شريك لك

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The testator asks God for help in distress, companionship in hardship, protection from the self, comfort in the grave, and a written covenant at the meeting with God.
rows.anchor: يا عدتي عند كربتي ويا صاحبي عند شدتي ويا ولي نعمتي وإلهي وإله آبائي لا تكلني إلى نفسي

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: The report connects the deathbed covenant to this verse and says making a will is every Muslim’s duty, which Muslims must preserve and teach.
rows.anchor: وتصديق هذه الوصية في سورة مريم في قوله لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمان عهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God took a child is attributed to Jews, Christians, and Arab polytheists: Jews named ʿUzayr, Christians the Messiah, and Arabs the angels.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار عن اليهود والنصارى ومشركي العرب فإن اليهود قالوا عزير ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they brought something hugely abominable and ugly; deleting the preposition bi makes the verb take its object directly.
rows.anchor: ها هنا حذف تقديره قل لهم يا محمد لقد جئتم بشيء منكر عظيم شنيع فظيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens nearly split, meaning they intended to split in horror at the enormity of the claim; were they to split for something great, this claim would warrant it.
rows.anchor: أي أرادت السماوات أن تنشق فعظم فريتهم إعظاما لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth nearly splits and the mountains nearly fall; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses hadda as severe breaking.
rows.anchor: أي كسرا شديدا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets hadda as demolition.
rows.anchor: شديدا عن ابن عباس. وقيل: هدما عن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An daʿaw is causal: the heavens, earth, and mountains nearly react because they ascribed a child to the Merciful, or because they named Him a child’s father.
rows.anchor: لأن دعوا للرحمان ولدا أو من دعوا للرحمان ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child is neither suitable nor fitting for the Merciful; having a child implies temporal origination and loss of divinity, and indicates need, so God is exalted above it.
rows.anchor: ما يصلح للرحمان ولا يليق به اتخاذ الولد وليس من صفته ذلك لأن إثبات الولد له يقتضي حدوثه

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: A report says ʿAlī repeated the Prophet’s prayer that God establish a covenant and place affection for him in believers’ hearts, after which this verse was revealed; similar is reported from Jābir.
rows.anchor: فقالهما علي ع فنزلت هذه الآية وروي نحوه عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري

rows.speaker: هرم بن حبان
rows.claim: Harm ibn Ḥayyān says when a servant turns his heart toward God, God turns believers’ hearts toward him and grants affection and mercy.
rows.anchor: ما أقبل عبد بقلبه إلى الله إلا أقبل الله بقلوب المؤمنين إليه حتى يرزقهم مودتهم

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas reports that God tells Gabriel He loves a believer; Gabriel and the heavens then love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth.
rows.anchor: إن الله إذا أحب مؤمنا قال لجبرائيل إني أحببت فلانا فأحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that interpretation, God loves believers and makes people love them.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون المعنى يحبهم الله ويحببهم إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God places love for believers in enemies’ and opponents’ hearts so they may enter the believers’ religion and gain strength through them.
rows.anchor: يجعل الله لهم محبة في قلوب أعدائهم ومخالفيهم ليدخلوا في دينهم ويعتزوا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that believers love one another, support one another, and unite against those who oppose them.
rows.anchor: يجعل بعضهم يحب بعضا فيكون كل واحد منهم عضدا لأخيه المؤمن

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says their mutual love will be in the Hereafter, like a parent’s love for a child, bringing complete joy and blessing.
rows.anchor: سيجعل لهم ودا في الآخرة فيحب بعضهم بعضا كمحبة الوالد لولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the first interpretation with ʿAlī’s authenticated saying: a believer will not hate him even if struck with a sword, while a hypocrite will not love him even if given the world.
rows.anchor: لو ضربت خيشوم المؤمن بسيفي هذا على أن يبغضني ما أبغضني

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement offered as support says no believer hates ʿAlī and no hypocrite loves him.
rows.anchor: لا يبغضك مؤمن ولا يحبك منافق

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says God made the Qurʾān easy by revealing it in the Prophet’s Arabic language so its hearers could understand it.
rows.anchor: يسرنا القرآن بأن أنزلناه بلسانك وهي لغة العرب ليسهل عليهم معرفته

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī alternatively says God made Qurʾānic recitation easy for the Prophet and enabled him to recite it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يسرناه قراءة القرآن على لسانك ومكناك من قراءته عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glad tidings are for those who avoid associating partners with God and major sins, informing them of what pleases them among God’s promises.
rows.anchor: الذين يتقون الشرك والكبائر أي تخبرهم بما تسرهم مما أعده الله لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ludd means fierce in dispute and identifies the people as Quraysh.
rows.anchor: شدادا في الخصومة عن ابن عباس يعني قريشا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets ludd as people given to argument and disputation.
rows.anchor: قوما ذوي جدل مخاصمين عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier generations were peoples who denied messengers; this history consoles the Prophet not to grieve over his opponents because the consequence returns to them.
rows.anchor: من قرن مكذبين للرسل وفيه تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى لا يهمنك كفرهم وشقاقهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda gloss taḥussu as seeing and rikzan as a sound.
rows.anchor: أي صوتا عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd gives ḥissan, a trace or sense, as an alternative gloss.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حسا عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed peoples left neither a visible person nor a sound, despite having more wealth, larger bodies, and fiercer disputes than present opponents; the same fate awaits these unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أكثر أموالا وأعظم أجساما وأشد خصاما من هؤلاء فلم يغنهم ذلك
